baseline_question: Which channels does the guide recommend for reporting a cyber attack to law enforcement?
ground_truth_context: Report to law enforcement Always remember that a cyber attack is a crime. Report to law enforcement via Report Fraud or through Police Scotland's 101 call centre. The NCSC strongly encourage the reporting of a cyber incident; many go unreported because of personal embarrassment.
ground_truth_answer: Report Fraud, or Police Scotland's 101 call centre.

baseline_question: What actions may be required when an organisation that manages its own IT activates its incident plan?
ground_truth_context: If you manage your own IT: put your plan into action. It's time to activate the incident plan you made in Step 1. Depending on the type of incident you are responding to, this may involve: replacing infected hardware; restoring services through backups; patching software; cleaning infected machines; changing passwords.
ground_truth_answer: Replacing infected hardware, restoring services through backups, patching software, cleaning infected machines, and changing passwords.

baseline_question: What is the difference between a hot debrief and a formal debrief?
ground_truth_context: There are two types of debriefs organisations may hold after experiencing a cybersecurity incident: a hot debrief and a formal debrief (or cold debrief). A hot debrief is held immediately after an organisation has recovered its networks and systems. A formal debrief is held days to weeks after an organisation has recovered its networks and systems.
ground_truth_answer: A hot debrief is held immediately after recovery; a formal debrief is held days to weeks afterwards.

baseline_question: How does the guidance define a cybersecurity incident?
ground_truth_context: An unwanted or unexpected cybersecurity event, or a series of such events, that either has compromised business operations or has a significant probability of compromising business operations.
ground_truth_answer: An unwanted or unexpected cybersecurity event, or a series of such events, that either has compromised business operations or has a significant probability of compromising them.

baseline_question: Which questions could a facilitator use to guide discussion during a hot debrief?
ground_truth_context: Content. The facilitator could guide discussion using the following questions: What went well? What could we do differently next time to improve? What action has been taken to remediate immediate risk? Are there any further issues that require immediate resolution?
ground_truth_answer: What went well; what could be done differently next time to improve; what action has been taken to remediate immediate risk; and whether any further issues require immediate resolution.

baseline_question: What reason does the publication give for no longer providing detailed incident response procedures?
ground_truth_context: The scope of this publication differs significantly from previous versions. Because the details of how to perform incident response activities change so often and vary so much across technologies, environments, and organizations, it is no longer feasible to capture and maintain that information in a single static publication.
ground_truth_answer: The details change too often and vary too much across technologies, environments and organisations to be captured in a single static publication.

baseline_question: Is incident response best handled as a separate set of activities performed by a separate team?
ground_truth_context: At that time, incidents were relatively rare, the scope of most incidents was narrow and well-defined, and incident response and recovery was usually completed within a day or two. Under those conditions, it was realistic to treat incident response as a separate set of activities performed by a separate team of personnel. However, the current state of incident response has greatly changed since then. Incident response is now considered a critical part of cybersecurity risk management that should be integrated across organizational operations.
ground_truth_answer: No. That was realistic when incidents were rare and narrow in scope. Incident response is now considered a critical part of cybersecurity risk management that should be integrated across organisational operations.

baseline_question: Which of the six CSF 2.0 Functions support preparation rather than incident response itself?
ground_truth_context: The bottom level reflects that the preparation activities of Govern, Identify, and Protect are not part of the incident response itself. Rather, they are much broader cybersecurity risk management activities that also support incident response. Incident response is shown in the top level of the figure: Detect, Respond, and Recover.
ground_truth_answer: Govern, Identify and Protect. Detect, Respond and Recover make up the incident response itself.

baseline_question: Which threats should a small organisation prepare for first?
ground_truth_context: So it is impractical to develop detailed step-by-step instructions to manage every type of incident, as the list could be endless. Instead you should prepare your business for the most common threats you face by developing plans to handle those incidents most likely to occur.
ground_truth_answer: The most common threats it faces, by developing plans for the incidents most likely to occur, rather than trying to cover every possible type of incident.

baseline_question: Where does the guide suggest looking for advice when trying to identify a cyber incident?
ground_truth_context: Use the information you have gathered to look for advice online from trusted sources such as police or security websites. You may be able to find instructions there on how to fix the problem, although care should be taken before acting on unverified advice. In the case of internet outage, contact your ISP (using the details you have already identified in your incident plan) in the first instance; most will have pages that relate to service availability.
ground_truth_answer: Trusted sources online such as police or security websites, with care taken before acting on unverified advice. For an internet outage, the ISP in the first instance.

baseline_question: What are the three actions that make up Drop, Cover, and Hold On?
ground_truth_context: Practice Drop, Cover, and Hold On with family and coworkers. Drop to your hands and knees. Cover your head and neck with your arms. Crawl only as far as needed to reach cover from falling materials. Hold on to any sturdy furniture until the shaking stops.
ground_truth_answer: Drop to your hands and knees; cover your head and neck with your arms; hold on to sturdy furniture until the shaking stops.

baseline_question: Is a doorway a recommended place to shelter during an earthquake?
ground_truth_context: IF AN EARTHQUAKE HAPPENS, PROTECT YOURSELF RIGHT AWAY. If in a vehicle, pull over and stop. If in bed, stay there. If outdoors, stay outdoors. Do not get in a doorway. Do not run outside.
ground_truth_answer: No. The sheet states that you should not get in a doorway.

baseline_question: What should someone do if an earthquake happens while they are in a vehicle?
ground_truth_context: If in a vehicle, stop in a clear area that is away from buildings, trees, overpasses, underpasses, or utility wires.
ground_truth_answer: Stop in a clear area away from buildings, trees, overpasses, underpasses and utility wires.

baseline_question: What should someone do if they become trapped in a building during a flood?
ground_truth_context: If trapped in a building, go to its highest level. Do not climb into a closed attic. You may become trapped by rising floodwater. Go on the roof only if necessary. Signal for help.
ground_truth_answer: Go to the highest level of the building, avoid a closed attic, go on the roof only if necessary, and signal for help.

baseline_question: Where can someone find information about the type of flood risk in their area?
ground_truth_context: Know your area's type of flood risk. Visit FEMA's Flood Map Service Center at https://msc.fema.gov/portal for information.
ground_truth_answer: FEMA's Flood Map Service Center.

baseline_question: Which shelter locations should be prioritized when a tornado warning is issued?
ground_truth_context: IF YOU ARE UNDER A TORNADO WARNING, FIND SAFE SHELTER RIGHT AWAY. Go to a safe room, basement, or storm cellar. If there is no basement, get to a small, interior room on the lowest level. Stay away from windows, doors, and outside walls.
ground_truth_answer: A safe room, basement or storm cellar first; if there is no basement, a small interior room on the lowest level, away from windows, doors and outside walls.

baseline_question: What signs may indicate that a tornado is approaching?
ground_truth_context: Know the signs of a tornado, including a rotating funnel-shaped cloud, an approaching cloud of debris, or a loud roar - similar to a freight train.
ground_truth_answer: A rotating funnel-shaped cloud, an approaching cloud of debris, or a loud roar similar to a freight train.

baseline_question: How does the guide recommend communicating with family and friends after a tornado?
ground_truth_context: Save your phone calls for emergencies. Phone systems are often down or busy after a disaster. Use text messaging or social media to communicate with family and friends.
ground_truth_answer: Save phone calls for emergencies because phone systems are often down or busy after a disaster, and use text messaging or social media instead.

baseline_question: What is the difference between a Flood Watch and a Flood Warning?
ground_truth_context: A Flood Warning is issued when the hazardous weather event is imminent or already happening. A Flood Watch is issued when conditions are favorable for flooding. It does not mean flooding will occur, but it is possible.
ground_truth_answer: A Flood Watch means conditions are favourable for flooding but it may not occur; a Flood Warning means flooding is imminent or already happening.

baseline_question: What action does the National Weather Service advise when a Flash Flood Warning is issued?
ground_truth_context: A Flash Flood Warning is issued when a flash flood is imminent or occurring. If you are in a flood prone area move immediately to high ground.
ground_truth_answer: Move immediately to high ground if you are in a flood prone area.

baseline_question: Is it safe to use a gas stove or oven to heat a home during a power outage?
ground_truth_context: Stay fire safe. Use flashlights, lanterns and other battery-powered lights. Don't use gas stoves or candles to heat your home. Never use a gas stovetop, oven, grill or dryer to heat your home. Always use fireplaces, portable heaters and wood-burning stoves safely.
ground_truth_answer: No. A gas stovetop, oven, grill or dryer must never be used to heat a home.

baseline_question: What precautions apply when using a vehicle as a source of power or warmth during an outage?
ground_truth_context: Don't leave a vehicle running inside a garage, even if the garage door is left open. If you use your vehicle as a source of power or warmth, make sure to run it in a well-ventilated place outside.
ground_truth_answer: Do not leave it running inside a garage even with the door open; run it in a well ventilated place outside.

baseline_question: What are the primary hazards to avoid when using a portable generator?
ground_truth_context: The primary hazards to avoid when using a generator are carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning from the toxic engine exhaust, electric shock or electrocution, fire and burns.
ground_truth_answer: Carbon monoxide poisoning from the engine exhaust, electric shock or electrocution, and fire and burns.

baseline_question: Is it safe to power house wiring by plugging a generator into a wall outlet?
ground_truth_context: NEVER try to power the house wiring by plugging the generator into a wall outlet, a practice known as backfeeding. This is extremely dangerous and presents an electrocution risk to utility workers and neighbors served by the same utility transformer. It also bypasses some of the built-in household circuit protection devices.
ground_truth_answer: No. This practice, called backfeeding, risks electrocuting utility workers and neighbours on the same transformer and bypasses built-in circuit protection.

baseline_question: How should fuel for a generator be stored?
ground_truth_context: Never store fuel for your generator in the home. Gasoline, propane, kerosene, and other flammable liquids should be stored outside of living areas in properly-labeled, non-glass safety containers. Do not store them near a fuel-burning appliance, such as a natural gas water heater in a garage.
ground_truth_answer: Outside living areas, in properly labelled non-glass safety containers, and not near a fuel-burning appliance. Never in the home.

baseline_question: What is the difference between refrigerated foods that must be discarded after a power outage and those that remain safe to eat?
ground_truth_context: Discard the following if your refrigerator has been without power for more than 4 hours: raw, cooked, or leftover meat, poultry, fish, eggs; luncheon meat; casseroles, soups, stews; mixed salads; gravy and stuffing; milk, cream, yogurt and soft cheeses; cut fruits and vegetables. Safe-to-eat foods: high-acid foods such as mustard, ketchup, relishes, pickles, jams and jellies; foods that do not require refrigeration, such as whole fresh fruits and vegetables, unopened juices, and dried fruits.
ground_truth_answer: Discard perishables such as meat, poultry, fish, eggs, dairy and cut produce after more than four hours without power. High-acid foods such as mustard, ketchup, pickles and jams, and foods that need no refrigeration such as whole fresh produce and unopened juices, remain safe.

baseline_question: Should perishable food be placed outside in the snow during a winter power outage?
ground_truth_context: During a snowstorm, do not place perishable food out in the snow. Outside temperatures can vary and food can be exposed to unsanitary conditions and animals. Instead, make ice. Fill buckets, empty milk containers, or cans with water and leave them outside to freeze.
ground_truth_answer: No. Outside temperatures vary and food can be exposed to unsanitary conditions and animals. Make ice instead by filling containers with water and leaving them outside to freeze.

baseline_question: What should be done in advance so that stored food stays safe if the power fails?
ground_truth_context: Keep an appliance thermometer in both the refrigerator and freezer. Group foods together in both the refrigerator and freezer. Keep the freezer full. Freeze refrigerated items that you may not need immediately.
ground_truth_answer: Keep an appliance thermometer in the refrigerator and freezer, group foods together, keep the freezer full, and freeze refrigerated items not needed immediately.

baseline_question: Where should someone look for official information during a power outage?
ground_truth_context: Listen closely to reports from officials and energy suppliers with battery-operated radios, computers, mobile phones, and other mobile devices. Newspapers and local media reports are other tools. Officials and energy suppliers should communicate basic information about what to do during an emergency and the status of restoration efforts.
ground_truth_answer: Reports from officials and energy suppliers, received through battery-operated radios, computers, mobile phones and other mobile devices, as well as newspapers and local media.

baseline_question: Which foods and utensils should be discarded after floodwater has entered a home?
ground_truth_context: Do not eat any food that may have come in contact with flood water. Discard any food that is not in a waterproof container. Also discard cardboard juice, milk and baby formula boxes and home canned foods. Inspect canned foods; discard any food in damaged cans. Discard wooden cutting boards, plastic utensils, baby bottle nipples, and pacifiers that may have come in contact with flood waters.
ground_truth_answer: Any food that may have touched floodwater, food not in a waterproof container, cardboard cartons, home canned foods, food in damaged cans, and wooden cutting boards, plastic utensils, baby bottle nipples and pacifiers.
